entries.text: What raw medium stock am I starting from?
Choose the extracellular molecule and concentration table.
A medium stock lists extracellular molecules and concentrations. Finite values cap availability; Infinity means the molecule is treated as unconstrained for the run.
A stock name such as MIX0-57.
Used as the base of a media recipe.
Do I need a new exchange molecule ID?
Use this only when a medium needs a molecule ID that the reconstruction does not already know. Most common metabolites are already registered.
Only if a new medium needs a new ID.
Those IDs can be used in media stocks and recipes.
How should this media recipe be assembled for experiments?
Choose or define the recipe operation: base stock, optional mixed stock, and ingredient additions or removals.
A recipe combines a base medium stock with supplements or ingredients and assigns one short ID, such as minimal_acetate. Downstream records use this recipe ID instead of the raw stock name.
A base medium and any ingredient IDs.
A recipe ID such as minimal_acetate.
Used as nutrients in growth conditions.
What biological growth condition should this recipe represent?
Attach biological context such as expected growth, TF lists, and genotype perturbations.
A growth condition ties a media recipe to expected growth behavior and regulatory state. This is what later appears as a selectable condition for experiments.
A recipe ID from Media Recipe.
A condition name, nutrients, TF lists, and doubling time.
Keeps TF rules aligned to the same setup.
Which TF state rules belong to this recipe?
Select reconstruction rules that explain active or inactive TF states.
These optional rows describe when a TF complex is active or inactive under nutrient contexts. They are not a free-form TF knockout; they encode reconstruction-level regulatory states.
The same recipe context used by the growth condition.
Finishes the regulatory context before building a protocol.
Does the environment stay constant or shift over time?
Choose a static medium or a time-ordered media-shift protocol.
A protocol is a time-ordered list of recipe changes, for example "0 minimal, 3600 minimal_acetate". The UI shows minutes and hours; published catalog rows store event times in seconds.
Recipe IDs; the first event should start from the current recipe.
1. What raw medium stock am I starting from?
Medium stock names come from files under condition/media. They are usually uppercase names such as MIX0-57 or MIX0-844.
Create a raw stock only when the reconstruction does not already contain the extracellular mixture you need.
Each row is one molecule available outside the cell. Use exact molecule IDs from the registry below; finite concentrations constrain availability, while
Use the file stem only, without .tsv. Repo convention here is usually uppercase names such as MY_NEW_MIX.
This creates a raw stock file under
. It is not experiment-selectable until a media recipe uses it.
Use this only for molecule IDs missing from the reconstruction registry. Existing catalog molecules can be added directly to the stock.
2. How should this media recipe be assembled for experiments?
Existing recipes are filtered so their base medium matches the selected medium stock. Supplement-only stocks will not show recipes until they are used through a base recipe.
No compatible media recipe is currently available for the selected medium stock.
A media recipe is an assembly operation, not just a name.
Start from one base stock, optionally mix in a supplement stock, then add or remove specific ingredients. The recipe ID is what growth conditions, media protocols, and experiments reference.
Use lowercase snake_case for named recipe IDs, for example minimal_acetate or my_new_media.
This is the stable ID users will later select in condition and protocol fields.
This should match a medium stock file name such as MIX0-57 or MY_NEW_MIX.
Use the stock that supplies the main extracellular composition.
Relative mixing volume for the base stock. Use 1.0 when this recipe uses only the base stock.
For a mixed recipe, this is the base stock fraction or volume used in the recipe.
Select an existing stock medium to mix with the base medium at the specified volume ratio, or choose None.

Use this for supplement stocks such as amino-acid mixes. Base stocks are model-valid mix-ins, but uncommon and should be used deliberately.

3. What biological growth condition should this recipe represent?
Existing growth conditions are filtered so their nutrients field matches the current media recipe.
No compatible growth condition is available for the current media recipe.
Create a growth condition only when you can justify the biological metadata.

The doubling time and TF lists are prior reconstruction metadata, not outputs calculated by this form. If they are unknown, reuse or fork the closest existing condition and edit only what is defensible.
Use lowercase snake_case, for example acetate, with_aa, or my_condition.
This name appears in experiment condition dropdowns after publish.
This should match the media recipe ID used by the growth condition, usually the recipe selected above.
This should be the media recipe whose biological context you are defining.
Measured or literature-supported expected doubling time in minutes. This is catalog metadata, not inferred by the builder.

4. Which TF state rules belong to this recipe?
Existing TF rules are filtered so either active nutrients or inactive nutrients matches the current media recipe.
No existing TF state rules match the current media recipe yet.
Create TF state rules only for reconstruction-level regulatory states you can justify.
These rows do not simulate a free-form TF knockout. They define when a TF complex is considered active or inactive under nutrient and optional genotype contexts.
These rows encode nutrient-dependent active and inactive TF states used by the reconstruction.
Short transcription-factor gene symbol, for example crp, fnr, or arcA.
Use a TF gene already present in the reconstruction rules.
Model complex or monomer ID for the active regulatory form.
Use a model complex or monomer ID already present in TF state rules.
Recipe context where this TF complex is considered active.
The media recipe under which the active state applies.
Contrasting recipe context where this TF complex is considered inactive.
The comparison recipe where the same TF rule is inactive.
Add known state ID forced to 0...

0CS = no sensor chemistry; 1CS = one-component sensor; 2CS = two-component phosphorelay.
Use the class that matches the TF mechanism encoded by the reconstruction.
5. Does the environment stay constant or shift over time?
Shifts into or otherwise involves selected recipe
Protocols are grouped by whether they start with the current recipe or shift into it later.
Protocol IDs usually start with a numeric prefix and then a short snake_case name, for example 000028_add_aa_long.
Controls the editable timeline horizon shown in this composer. The published catalog row stores event times in seconds, but users should set the range in hours.
This is only the composer horizon. It is not the simulation division timeout from Design Experiment.

Build reusable experiment environments by answering five connected questions: starting stock, named media recipe, growth condition, TF state rules, and media protocol. Published records appear as selectable options when designing simulations.
